NEW src/engine/adr-scaffold.ts. root discovery, max+1 allocation, §4.1 template rendering, `project.architecture.decisions` honoured with a `docs/decisions` default (FR-002, FR-003, FR-019). Tests: src/engine/adr-scaffold.test.ts

REVIEW FAIL (uat): US-001 concurrent allocation — Expected: two concurrent `gwrk define adr` runs compute the same number and the second fails loudly with `ADR-NNN already exists: docs/decisions/<path>` and exit 1 (FR-002, TC-015). Actual: reproduced 5/5 against a corpus of ADR-001 — both runs exited 0 and wrote `ADR-002-alpha-one.md` and `ADR-002-beta-two.md`, the silent-sibling flaw FR-002 names as the second flaw of the research allocator. See spec.md > US-001, FR-002 Error States, TC-015. Root cause: in `scaffold()` (src/engine/adr-scaffold.ts) both processes complete the `readRecordEntries` re-read before either writes, so the check sees no conflict, and the `wx` flag only refuses an identical filename — a different slug at the same number passes. Fix: make the number claim atomic rather than check-then-write. Create the record with `flag: "wx"` at the allocated number FIRST, then on `EEXIST` re-read and retry the allocation (or fail naming the conflicting path); alternatively scan for any `ADR-NNN-*.md` immediately after the write and refuse if a second one is present. Add a non-mocked regression to src/engine/adr-scaffold.test.ts that drives two overlapping `scaffold()` calls against a real temp directory and asserts exactly one record exists at the number and the loser rejects — the existing mocked-fs test forces a state the real filesystem sequence never produces, which is why this shipped green.

REVIEW FAIL (code): TC-015 departure is undocumented in every commitment that names it — FR-002, TC-015.
  WHERE: src/engine/adr-scaffold.ts:22-28,98-137,253-261,338-421 ; specs/029-decision-records/spec.md:464 ; specs/029-decision-records/contracts/adr-engine.md:154-158,195 ; specs/029-decision-records/plan.md:197,843
  EXPECTED: The three commitments describing this module agree with the module. spec.md:464 TC-015 says "No locking ... A lockfile is out of proportion to a human-paced command". contracts/adr-engine.md:156 says allocateNumber is "Max+1 over entries matching /^ADR-(\d{3})-/ ... No locking (TC-015)". contracts/adr-engine.md:195 fixes the order as findProjectRoot -> resolveDecisionsDir -> allocateNumber -> existence check -> mkdir -> writeFile. plan.md:197 and plan.md:843 both record TC-015 as "Honoured — existence check, no lockfile".
  ACTUAL: The module ships a lock file. scaffold() at adr-scaffold.ts:374-421 runs mkdir -> claimNumber -> existence check -> writeFile, and claimNumber at :115-137 publishes a `.ADR-NNN.claim` with an atomic fs.link, released in a finally. allocateNumber at :253-261 counts claim files as held numbers, not just records matching the contracted pattern. No spec, plan or contract text records any of this. plan.md's own convention is that a departure from the spec's literal text is recorded in "Resolved Ambiguities" (AMBER-1, AMBER-2); this is a third departure and it is recorded only in a source comment at adr-scaffold.ts:22-28.
  FIX: Do NOT revert the claim mechanism. It is correct and it is the only thing that satisfies FR-002. Verified this review: 5/5 two-process races on a real filesystem land exactly one ADR-002, the loser exits 1 with `ADR-002 already exists: docs/decisions/ADR-002-<slug>.md`, and no claim or stage file is left behind. TC-015 as written is self-contradictory — check-then-write cannot produce the loud second failure FR-002 requires, because both runs finish reading before either writes. Record the departure instead, in four places: (1) add an AMBER entry to plan.md "Resolved Ambiguities" stating that TC-015's no-lockfile prohibition cannot deliver FR-002's stated outcome and that a released-on-exit `.ADR-NNN.claim` published by fs.link is taken in its place; (2) amend spec.md:464 TC-015 to permit the atomic claim and keep the prohibition on a lock manager, daemon, timeout or retry loop; (3) amend contracts/adr-engine.md:156 so allocateNumber's contract states that a number held by a claim counts as held, and :195 so the order of operations is the one the code runs; (4) correct plan.md:197 and plan.md:843, which currently assert "no lockfile" about code that has one.
  GATE: none — the task gateScript (build, adr-scaffold/adr/cli.ux/cli.e2e/cli.option-collisions suites, define --help greps) passes in full, and T008-gate.sh passes. No assertion in it compares the shipped mechanism against the contract text, which is the coverage hole. Add a gate line that fails when contracts/adr-engine.md still reads "No locking" while adr-scaffold.ts contains fs.link.
  REF: plan.md Phase 2 > Governance & Skills Contract (TC-015 row); plan.md > Resolved Ambiguities; spec.md > 6. Technical Constraints > TC-015

REVIEW FAIL (code): PROMPT.md describes a template shape the scaffold does not write — FR-003, FR-007.
  WHERE: src/plugins/builtins/workflows/gwrk-adr-record/PROMPT.md:6-8, :20-21, :35-41
  EXPECTED: The prompt must describe the record renderTemplate() actually writes. src/engine/adr-scaffold.ts:284-339 emits SEVEN numbered sections (## 1. Context, ## 2. Decision, ## 3. Decision Record, ## 4. Alternatives Rejected, ## 5. Impact on Existing Code, ## 6. Consequences, ## 7. References) plus the unnumbered `## Amendments` registry table, which FR-003 mandates and src/engine/adr-scaffold.test.ts:428,460-474 asserts.
  ACTUAL: Line 7 says "the file already exists with its number, its `Status: Proposed` header and its six empty sections". The Algorithm step 4 fill-list (lines 35-41) stops at `## 6. Consequences`. `## 7. References` and `## Amendments` are named nowhere in the prompt, while step 6 (line 43) instructs "Emit one WRITE_FILE intent carrying the complete record for the target path" — a full-file replacement of the scaffold.
  IMPACT: `gwrk define adr "<title>" --run` is this phase's primary path. WorkflowRuntime executes the WRITE_FILE intent (src/plugins/workflow-runtime.ts:530-533) and its wouldShrinkExistingFile guard only rejects SMALLER content, so a filled record missing `## 7. References` and `## Amendments` lands on disk. That record fails FR-003's shape, and Phase 8 `--amend` / FR-022 (`grep '^## Amendments'`) plus FR-021's max+1 scan over `## N.` headings have nothing to resolve against.
  FIX: In PROMPT.md change "six empty sections" to "seven numbered sections and an empty `## Amendments` registry". Add `## 7. References` to the step-4 fill-list ("specs, research and prior records this decision rests on"). Add an explicit Scope Constraint: "MUST reproduce `## 7. References` and the trailing unnumbered `## Amendments` heading with its empty three-column table. The registry is written by `--amend`, never by you — emit it empty."
  GATE: Phase 3 Done-When block (task gateScript) — NOT covered. Its only PROMPT.md assertion is the TC-008 placeholder check `if grep -qE '\{\{[A-Z_]+\}\}' … then exit 1; fi`. Nothing asserts the prompt agrees with renderTemplate(), so the gate is green over this defect. Add: `grep -q '## 7. References' src/plugins/builtins/workflows/gwrk-adr-record/PROMPT.md` and `grep -q '## Amendments' src/plugins/builtins/workflows/gwrk-adr-record/PROMPT.md`.
  REF: plan.md Phase 3 > Files; spec.md FR-003 (:339), FR-007 (:343); contracts/adr-command.md §3

REVIEW FAIL (code): `pnpm lint` fails on adr.ts — implicit `any` in the dispatch path — FR-007.
  WHERE: src/commands/adr.ts:113, :114, :118, :125, and :185-195 (formatter)
  EXPECTED: `pnpm lint` (`biome check`) exits 0 on src/commands/adr.ts, as it did before this phase. Verified: the HEAD~1 version of this file produces zero biome lint diagnostics.
  ACTUAL: Four lint errors plus a formatter diff, all inside the Phase 3 addition:
    - :125 `lint/suspicious/noImplicitAnyLet` — `let workflowResult;` has no type annotation and no initializer, so it is implicitly `any`. This is the non-test critical dispatch path, and it defeats the type check on the `workflowResult?.summary` / `workflowResult.intents` guard at :144-151. NOT auto-fixable.
    - :113, :114, :118 `lint/style/noUnusedTemplateLiteral` — backtick literals with no interpolation in the `workflowInput` array. `biome lint --write` does NOT fix these (biome 1.9.4 classes the fix unsafe); they need `--unsafe` or a hand edit.
    - :185-195 formatter — `.option("--run", "Draft the scaffolded record with the gwrk-adr-record workflow")` and the `.action(async (title: string | undefined, opts: {...}) => {` signature both exceed the line width and must be wrapped.
  FIX: Change :125 to `let workflowResult: Awaited<ReturnType<WorkflowRuntime["executeWorkflow"]>>;` (or declare it as the imported `WorkflowResult` type). Change the three empty backtick literals at :113, :114, :118 to `""`. Run `pnpm exec biome format --write src/commands/adr.ts` for the wrapping. Re-verify with `pnpm exec biome check src/commands/adr.ts`.
  GATE: Phase 3 Done-When block (task gateScript) — NOT covered. The gate runs `pnpm run build` (tsc only) and vitest. `let x;` is an evolving-any that tsc accepts under `strict`, so the compile gate cannot see it, and no gate line runs biome. The gate is green over this defect. Add `pnpm exec biome check src/commands/adr.ts` to the Done-When block.
  REF: plan.md Phase 3 > Files > `src/commands/adr.ts`; biome.json (`linter.rules.recommended: true`, `suspicious.noExplicitAny: "error"`)

REVIEW FAIL (code): `--run` calls loadConfig with the working directory, not the project root — FR-007, FR-002, SC-001.
  WHERE: src/commands/adr.ts:98 and :105 (`draftRecord`), relative to :107
  EXPECTED: The project root walk resolves BEFORE the config read, and both config lookups receive it:
      const projectRoot = await findProjectRoot(cwd);
      const config = loadConfig(projectRoot);
      const backend = config.agents?.define;
      ...
      const model = resolveModelForTask("define", backend, projectRoot);
    `loadConfig(projectRoot)` reads `path.join(projectRoot, ".gwrkrc.json")` and does NOT walk parents (src/utils/config.ts:315-321). `findProjectRoot` (src/engine/adr-scaffold.ts:201-218) is the walk FR-002 mandates, and it is already imported and already called at :107.
  ACTUAL: :98 `const config = loadConfig(cwd);` and :105 `resolveModelForTask("define", backend, cwd)` both take the raw working directory. `const projectRoot = await findProjectRoot(cwd);` is computed at :107, two statements too late, and is used only for the `executeWorkflow` options.
  REPRODUCED: project at /tmp/adrrepro with `.gwrkrc.json` carrying `agents.define: "claude"`; handler driven with `cwd` = /tmp/adrrepro/sub/deeper and `run: true`.
    - scaffold succeeded and wrote /tmp/adrrepro/docs/decisions/ADR-001-repro-from-subdir.md (the walk works)
    - the handler then threw: `Configuration file .gwrkrc.json not found at /tmp/adrrepro/sub/deeper/.gwrkrc.json. Run 'gwrk init' to initialize this project.`
    - direct probe of the built `loadConfig`: `/tmp/adrrepro` -> OK (agents.define = claude); `/tmp/adrrepro/sub/deeper` -> THROW, same message.
  IMPACT: `gwrk define adr "<title>" --run` fails from every subdirectory of the project. US-001 acceptance scenario 3 (spec.md:89) and SC-001 (spec.md:500) both require the command to work from any subdirectory, and FR-002 (spec.md:338) exists specifically to fix the research allocator's habit of joining `process.cwd()` with literals — this reintroduces it one layer up. The failure is also partial-state and mis-signposted: the record IS written, then the user is told to run `gwrk init` on an already-initialized project. That message is a fourth error state absent from the FR-007 Error States table (spec.md:354-359). `resolveModelForTask` carries the same defect silently: `loadRegistry(cwd)` is caught and returns `undefined` (src/utils/resolve-model.ts:26-37), so a project-local model registry is invisible from a subdirectory and `model` is dropped from the dispatch — the exact class of invisibility this phase passes `projectRoot` to `executeWorkflow` to avoid.
  FIX: In `draftRecord` (src/commands/adr.ts:91-154), hoist `const projectRoot = await findProjectRoot(cwd);` from :107 to above :98, then change :98 to `loadConfig(projectRoot)` and :105 to `resolveModelForTask("define", backend, projectRoot)`. Delete the now-duplicate :107. Order is load-bearing: the root walk must throw its own `Not a gwrk project: no .gwrkrc.json found in <cwd> or any parent. Run: gwrk init` (the declared error state at spec.md:350) before any config read.
  GATE: Phase 3 Done-When block (task gateScript) — NOT covered, gate is GREEN over this defect. Verified: all ten gate lines pass and all 59 tests in the four phase suites pass. `src/commands/adr-dispatch.test.ts:44-51` mocks BOTH `../engine/adr-scaffold.js` (so `findProjectRoot` returns a constant "/repo") and `../utils/config.js` (so `loadConfig` is `vi.fn(() => ({agents:{define:"claude"}}))`, which ignores its argument entirely). No mock can observe which path the real `loadConfig` receives. Add an assertion that `loadConfig` and `resolveModelForTask` are each called with the value `findProjectRoot` returned, not with `cwd`:
    expect(vi.mocked(loadConfig)).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/repo");
    expect(vi.mocked(resolveModelForTask)).toHaveBeenCalledWith("define", "claude", "/repo");
  drive it with `adrCommandHandler({ target: "Decision Records", run: true, cwd: "/repo/src/deep" })` so cwd and projectRoot differ.
  REF: plan.md Phase 3 > Files > `src/commands/adr.ts`; spec.md FR-007 (:343), FR-002 (:338), US-001 AC-3 (:89), SC-001 (:500), FR-007 Error States (:354); contracts/adr-command.md §3

REVIEW FAIL (code): resolveDecisionsDir swallows a real config error and silently writes to the wrong directory — FR-019, TC-002.
  WHERE: src/engine/adr-scaffold.ts:230-247 (the catch at :242-244) ; src/engine/adr-scaffold.test.ts:525-535

REVIEW FAIL (uat): US-001 / FR-003 today's date — Expected: the record's `> **Date:**` field holds the author's local calendar date (FR-003 "today's date", US-001 "Status: Proposed and today's date"). Actual: reproduced on the built CLI at 2026-08-30 20:59 MDT — `gwrk define adr "Timezone Probe"` wrote `> **Date:** 2026-08-31`, one day ahead of the author's today. Every record authored after 18:00 in America/Denver (17:00 Pacific) is stamped tomorrow, a six-to-seven hour window each day. Corpus ordering also stops being monotonic: a record authored at 19:00 on the 30th outranks one authored at 09:00 on the 31st, and `Date:` is the only ordering signal a reader has once numbers are allocated by a race. See spec.md > US-001, FR-003. Root cause: `scaffold()` at src/engine/adr-scaffold.ts:426 passes `date: new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` into `renderTemplate` — `toISOString()` is UTC, not local. Fix: build the date from local components instead, e.g. `new Date().toLocaleDateString("en-CA")` (which yields YYYY-MM-DD) or an explicit `getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate` join. Test coverage hole: src/engine/adr-scaffold.test.ts:431 ("FR-003: stamps today's date, not a hardcoded one") injects `date: "2026-08-20"` into `renderTemplate` and only asserts it renders, so it never exercises the call that chooses the date. Add a test that fakes a clock at a local time whose UTC date differs (e.g. `vi.setSystemTime` at 2026-08-30T23:00 in a UTC-6 TZ) and asserts `scaffold()` writes the local date, not the UTC one. Add a gate line that runs the built CLI under `TZ=America/Denver` and fails when the written `> **Date:**` value does not equal `TZ=America/Denver date +%Y-%m-%d`. Note: src/engine/plan-renderer.ts:33 has the same UTC-for-a-human-date call; fixing it is out of Phase 2 scope but worth filing.
